observations: The three GPU drivers give the same error maxima in each precision.
The cloudy-sky differences against native main McICA are reproduced with CPU McICA ACC: these runs use different cloud-sampling algorithms and are not paired numerical regressions.
All six GPU outputs pass nccmp against the new CPU McICA ACC net-flux outputs with longwave threshold 0.001 and shortwave threshold 0.1 W/m2, including single precision.
No comparison thresholds or reference files have been relaxed.

diagnostic_fixes: Use main's pointer-aware NetCDF input reader for CPU and accelerator drivers.
Build the legacy driver-dependent GPU blocking module in a separate driver-side object library.
Use ordered per-column band/canopy aggregation without temporary index-array mappings; preserve pointer strides with assumed-shape arguments.
Wait inside aggregation helpers to keep call-local descriptors alive until their asynchronous launches finish; global forced synchronization is not used in the successful smoke job.
Offload the nearest-band shortwave surface-albedo path used by main's configuration; previously that path only populated host scratch.
Make gang-private scratch explicit on the OpenACC parallel construct in the legacy McICA and direct-aerosol kernels, allowing those units to compile with the diagnostic flags.
Wait for queue 1 before diagnostic host copies and after pointer-component host updates, so saved radiative properties observe completed preparation.
remaining_build_issues: Inherited NVHPC inline-library extraction remains unresolved; correctness builds explicitly disable it. No performance conclusion is drawn from these builds.
A separate O0 diagnostic run stopped at an unmapped cloud-optics scratch array, before the later spectral aggregation stage.
OpenMP-target compilation and device validation have not yet run.
